goal: Let DC-Agent memory and operating rules grow in a controlled spiral: task experience becomes reviewed memory, repeated approved memory becomes a SOP upgrade proposal, and Subagent-Driven verification gates every runtime rule change.

acceptance_criteria.description: Content SOP task payloads carry a spiral_evolution seed that records the workflow scope, autonomous actions, human-gated actions, and Subagent-Driven requirement.

A generated Content SOP result creates a need_review memory candidate with source_task_id, department_id, scenario_id, source_citations, and an Obsidian governance target; it must not promote directly to runtime.
Only repeated approved experiences can become a stable SOP upgrade proposal; unapproved or low-support corrections stay below the runtime-change threshold.

Every SOP upgrade proposal includes a Subagent-Driven plan with implementer, spec compliance reviewer, code quality reviewer, verification runner, targeted gate, and repository hygiene gates before runtime application.
Content SOP settlement attaches the spiral evolution snapshot to review_required results so employee review, memory governance, and SOP upgrade proposals stay traceable from the harness task.

Only explicit approved_for_runtime stable SOP proposals can be applied to the versioned content_sop_rule_overrides runtime file; pending, unreviewed, or generic approved proposals must not write runtime rules.
Applying an approved SOP proposal is idempotent and writes a versioned audit record without duplicating rules for the same proposal_id.
Content SOP payloads hot-read matching enabled runtime rule overrides and append them to truth_requirements without changing static department workflow defaults.
Runtime SOP rule overrides are rollbackable by proposal_id; disabled rules no longer affect future Content SOP payloads.
Malformed or schema-invalid content_sop_rule_overrides config fails closed instead of silently dropping or overwriting runtime rules.
Runtime override backups and temporary files are kept outside data/config so sensitive SOP rule backups are not accidentally staged as config files.
Stable Content SOP rule proposals have a persisted review store with pending, approved_for_runtime, applied, rejected, and rolled_back states plus append-only audit events.
The Feishu review plugin rejects untrusted hand-written card actions and non-admin reviewers before approving, applying, or rolling back runtime SOP rules.
The Feishu review plugin uses a two-step apply/rollback confirmation flow: approve sends a confirm card, confirm applies the versioned override, and rollback confirm disables the rule.
Obsidian governance import can draft pending Content SOP rule proposals from repeated approved governed process memories, while keeping runtime application behind the Feishu human review plugin.
Successful Content SOP settlement exports its spiral memory candidate as a need_review governed memory note in Obsidian Inbox, without making it eligible for default runtime recall before approval.

Content SOP ops runtime summarizes pending rule proposals, approved-but-unapplied proposals, runtime overrides, governed memory queues, quality scores, and operating SOP recommendations for a full-chain dashboard.
Content SOP ops runtime builds proactive Feishu/admin reminder cards for pending approvals, approved-but-unapplied runtime rules, need_review memories, and blocked quality gates.
Content SOP ops has a runtime scheduled-run entrypoint that plans governance import/export work and exports append-only audit reports without relying on test-only scripts.
Content SOP ops exposes dashboard API routes for full-chain status and scheduled audit execution.

Content SOP production readiness confirmation verifies admin reviewers, Feishu reminders, scheduled import/export, audit reports, quality score policy, governed memory paths, and Obsidian vault availability.
Employee chat can produce a low-friction SOP signal only when the message contains reusable operating intent and workflow scope; one-off wording edits must not become SOP candidates.
Employee-facing SOP signal confirmation avoids SOP jargon, gives simple choices, and creates only a need_review process memory candidate with Obsidian governance as the promotion gate.
Rule proposal readiness diagnostics explain eligible support, missing scope, unapproved evidence, and remaining support needed before any runtime SOP proposal is drafted.

The DC router detects employee SOP signals on managed Feishu messages, sends a trusted low-friction confirmation card, and only after a remember action exports an auto-approved governed memory plus Obsidian governance note without applying runtime rules.

autonomy_policy.hard_rule: Memory can grow automatically; runtime thinking rules require approved memory, Subagent-Driven review, passing tests, and repository hygiene.

non_goals: Do not let AI modify router, harness, department workflow, or prompt rules without review.
Do not promote need_review memory into runtime recall.
Do not treat a single employee complaint as a permanent company SOP.
Do not bypass Obsidian memory governance.
Do not bypass scripts/agent-check.sh --profile targeted and repository hygiene checks for runtime rule changes.
